question: Assume today is 2026-08-17. You know nothing published after this date. Estimate the seasonally adjusted annual rate of privately-owned housing starts in the United States in August 2026 (the number of housing units at an annual rate, as in '1,300,000'), as it will be first reported in the U.S. Census Bureau and HUD Monthly New Residential Construction release.

target.what: Seasonally adjusted annual rate of privately-owned housing starts in the United States for August 2026, as first reported in the Census Bureau/HUD Monthly New Residential Construction release (units started during the month, expressed at an annual rate)
target.publisher: U.S. Census Bureau and U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development (HUD)
target.cadence: monthly, released mid-month for the prior month (August 2026 data would first be published around mid-September 2026)
target.caveats: Target period is future relative to the 2026-08-17 cutoff, so no August 2026 observation exists; must be forecast from pre-cutoff signals. 'Privately-owned' excludes public housing starts (small share). 'Housing starts' counts units on which construction has begun, not permits or completions. SAAR i

candidates.hypothesis: Recent monthly private housing starts SAAR (through June/July 2026) plus seasonal and trend patterns anchor a short-horizon forecast; August typically shows a modest seasonal-adjustment-neutral move from July.
candidates.data_to_find: Monthly private housing starts SAAR for Jan 2024 through the latest month published before 2026-08-17 (likely June or July 2026), plus single-family vs 5+ unit split and month-over-month changes; also August values in prior years for seasonal context.
search_hints: Census Bureau new residential construction housing starts June 2026
privately owned housing starts SAAR July 2026

candidates.hypothesis: Permits precede starts; the permit-to-start ratio is fairly stable over 1-3 months, so recent permit levels (especially single-family) constrain August starts.
candidates.data_to_find: Monthly building permits SAAR (total and single-family) for months through mid-2026, and the historical permits-to-starts ratio; minimum: latest 3-6 months of permit data.

candidates.hypothesis: Units under construction and completions reflect the pipeline; a large under-construction backlog with declining completions implies starts momentum, while a shrinking pipeline implies weakness.
candidates.data_to_find: Housing units under construction (monthly, through mid-2026) and completions SAAR; historical relationship between under-construction stock and starts.

candidates.hypothesis: Published forecasts or nowcasts for August 2026 housing starts (or Q3 2026) provide a direct anchor; treat as forecast, not observation.
candidates.data_to_find: Any pre-cutoff forecasts for August/Q3 2026 housing starts from banks, Fannie Mae, NAHB, or nowcasting services; also NAHB/Wells Fargo housing market index and single-family starts expectations.

candidates.hypothesis: Mortgage rates, Fed policy, and builder sentiment drive single-family starts with a lag; a rate environment shift in mid-2026 changes the August level.
candidates.data_to_find: 30-year mortgage rate path through mid-2026, Fed funds expectations, builder sentiment (NAHB HMI) monthly through mid-2026, and any housing policy changes.

candidates.hypothesis: Multifamily (5+ unit) starts are volatile and regionally concentrated; separating single-family (stable) from multifamily (lumpy) improves the forecast, since August multifamily could swing the total.
candidates.data_to_find: Regional housing starts (Northeast, Midwest, South, West) and multifamily starts for recent months; multifamily permit trends and apartment completions.

candidates.hypothesis: August unadjusted starts and the Census seasonal factors determine the SAAR; knowing the typical August seasonal factor and unadjusted August level helps translate any unadjusted signal.
candidates.data_to_find: Census seasonal adjustment factors for housing starts by month, and historical August unadjusted-to-adjusted ratios.
search_hints: Census housing starts seasonal adjustment factors

methods.rationale: Anchors on the latest observed total starts (June 2026, 1,427,000) and applies a change factor to August 2026. The factor accounts for the likely partial reversal of June's multifamily spike and weak builder sentiment, with a wide range for multifamily volatility. Shared dependency: relies on June being a representative base; failure mode is an unobserved July/August multifamily swing.

by_construction: Only URLs leave the searcher (code regex); extractor, judge and final prompts never contain search result titles, snippets or the searcher's text. This holds by construction and is not measured.
residual_risks: The searcher sees post-cutoff search results and chooses which URLs are fetched, so page selection can be conditioned on the answer; only the URLs leave the searcher, and in backtests every fetched page is a snapshot dated <= as_of.
Live pages are used only when as_of is today; in backtests every page is an archived snapshot dated <= as_of.
The leak sentinel only catches registered official values in common formats, not paraphrased or derived numbers.
The model's own training data (knowledge cutoff unpublished) can include history before as_of; it cannot include the target if the target was published after the model's release.
Wayback snapshots are captured by a third party; a snapshot date <= as_of proves the content existed by then.
Assumption values are proposed by the judge model from its own knowledge, which can include the target's history before as_of; code checks their form, not where the number came from.
